column4: Today you will learn three things.
Now for the sound of the day.
Listen for it in these words.
This is how we write it.
Now Bloop will talk to you. When Bloop speaks, you answer.
Time to sing. The first time, just listen and clap.
Spot the word. Listen, then point to the word you hear.
Look at everything you can do now.
Bloop is saying hello in Spanish. By the end of today, you will too.
I can say hello and goodbye in Spanish.
I can answer yes or no.
I can say the Spanish a and o sounds.
In Spanish, the letter a always makes the same short, open sound.
Open your mouth wide, like the start of the word father, and keep it short.
The letter o makes a round sound.
Make your lips round, like you are blowing out a candle, and keep them still.
Look at the first word. The h is a sleeping letter, so we never say it.
This one means yes. Nod your head as you say it.
And this one means no. Keep your lips round and still.
Spot the upside down mark at the start? Spanish puts one there, so you know how to say it before you begin.
A question gets an upside down mark too. Listen.
Thumbs up. Is that yes or no?
Now you start. Say good morning to Bloop.
Now for five new words. Watch Bloop, and copy.
Your job for home: tonight, teach someone at home how to say hello, good morning and goodbye in Spanish.
Bloop is saying hello in French. By the end of today, you will too.
I can say hello and goodbye in French.
I can hear the French sound i.
In French, the letter i makes a short, bright sound. The letter y can make it too.
Smile wide, as if someone is taking your photo, and keep the sound short.
Now for three new words. Watch Bloop, and copy.
Our first word means hello. You can use it all day long.
This one means thank you. Can you hear the bright i at the end?
This is a polite hello for a grown up.
And with your friends, you can say this.
Bloop gives you a present. What do you say?
Now you start. Say goodbye to Bloop.
Your job for home: tonight, teach someone at home how to say hello, thank you and goodbye in French.
